title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski reflects on Falcons matchup versus Kansas City | Press Conference
headline: Stefanski stuck with Michael Penix Jr. after a sloppy home loss to Kansas City. Harold Perkins drew strong praise, and Bijan Robinson's usage is tied to the passing game.
summary: Stefanski said Atlanta lost to a good Kansas City team because it did not play clean football. The offense had early three-and-outs, failed to sustain drives and could not convert third downs, and the offensive line had pre-snap penalties for a second straight week. He took responsibility himself and said the team's fight is not in question. He said he is still confident in Michael Penix Jr., who has struggled since Week 8, and said the offense needs more precision in the run and pass game to avoid third downs. A fourth-and-four failure in the third quarter was a turning point, but he said he liked the process behind it and would need to watch the tape on the Penix-to-Pitts throw. He praised linebacker Harold Perkins for his play, especially on third down. He also explained that Bijan Robinson's early touches came from both the Chiefs' strong run defense and the plan to use him in the pass game. With the bye coming, he said he reviews everything every week, including personnel and play calling, and did not rule out changes. He said new starters Corey Levin and DeMarcco Hellams mostly did their jobs.

signals.claim: Penix remains the starting quarterback, and Stefanski expects the offense to improve
signals.note: Penix has been shaky since Week 8, but the coach publicly backed him and put the blame on himself rather than the QB.
signals.quote: Confident Mike, he'll be better.

signals.claim: Perkins is playing at a high level and will keep a significant defensive role
signals.note: He was singled out for his play, especially on third down, which is good for IDP value.
signals.quote: get to the quarterback was outstanding

signals.claim: Robinson will be used as a pass-game target as well as a runner, depending on how defenses play Atlanta
signals.note: He had one carry in the first two series. The coach framed that as the game plan and a tough run defense, which keeps his receiving role in play.
signals.quote: somebody that you're trying to get the ball to.

signals.claim: Levin made his first start on the offensive line and mostly played acceptably
signals.note: The line was a problem with penalties, so his hold on a starting spot is uncertain, and the coach said he will examine personnel.
signals.quote: by and large those guys did their job

signals.claim: Hellams made his first start in the secondary and mostly played acceptably
signals.note: He is a new starter, but the coach's review was lukewarm and he said he needs to watch the tape.
signals.quote: by and large those guys did their job

topics.detail: Atlanta had four straight three-and-outs to open the game and has been slow in first quarters this season. Stefanski wants more precision in the run and pass game to avoid third downs and convert the manageable ones.
The offensive line was flagged for a second straight week, mostly for false starts. Stefanski called it a point of emphasis and said the team needs to carry its practice work into games.

Tommy Rees worked from the sideline this week to improve communication with new faces on the roster. Stefanski took responsibility for the offense, said he looks at everything weekly, and did not give a direct vote of confidence on the play calling.
Stefanski said the team has not given up on the season and is focused on the next game. He did not say whether the division race is still realistic.

title: Joe Brady On Bills Explosive Plays, Improving Defense, And More In Victory Over Jets
headline: Bills beat the Jets 31-12 on second-half quick strikes. James Cook broke a 74-yard TD, Spencer Brown played after being listed doubtful, and new S Amani Hooker played the whole game.
summary: Joe Brady said the Bills struggled in the first half, with too many pre-snap penalties and missed chances, but responded after halftime. They scored on opening drives of two, four and one play by leaning on tempo. He credited earlier physical games, especially the Monday night game, for wearing the Jets down late. He praised the defense for strong communication and for holding the Jets to 12 points, and singled out Amani Hooker for playing the whole game after only a walk-through on Wednesday. Spencer Brown was listed doubtful but tested out well on gameday morning and held up well against Jets EDGE David Bailey. Brady said James Cook's 74-yard touchdown came from patience in the run scheme and Cook's confidence once he got to the second level. He also praised DJ Moore's toughness and said rookie TJ Parker's reps will keep rising. Brady called this the team's best win of the season given the short week and travel, and the team is 8-1.

injuries.detail: Listed doubtful with an ankle injury. He felt better after a workout Sunday morning and played, effectively against Jets EDGE David Bailey, without practicing during the week.
Did not practice but did a Wednesday walk-through, including the two-minute drill. He played the entire game and nearly had a couple of interceptions.

signals.claim: Hooker will be a significant contributor in the Bills' secondary going forward
signals.note: A newly added safety who played every snap with almost no practice, which points to a major defensive role and IDP value.
signals.quote: I'm so impressed with Amani Hooker.

signals.claim: Brown will play through injuries without practicing if he feels able to go
signals.note: He played after being listed doubtful, so his ankle is a manageable concern and the protection for Josh Allen stays intact.
signals.quote: we were leaning towards him not being able to play

signals.claim: Cook will keep getting patient carries in the scheme, with chances for big plays like the 74-yard TD
signals.note: His breakout run shows his ceiling in an offense that sticks with the run, though yardage can come in clumps.
signals.quote: eventually it's going to break to a 74 yarder

signals.note: Brady trusts Moore on tempo and big-play opportunities and praised his toughness, which supports his steady role.
signals.quote: he's everything we want on this football team

signals.claim: Parker's snaps and reps will continue to increase
signals.note: The rookie pass rusher is developing and producing sacks, so his role is growing as an edge rusher.
signals.quote: his reps are going to continue to go up

topics.detail: Brady said there were too many pre-snap penalties and missed first-half chances, and the team must play cleaner football.
The Bills changed the tempo in the second half and scored on two-, four- and one-play drives, which Brady said benefited the offense after 80-play games recently.

Brady said defensive communication and understanding of the scheme are at a high level after the bye. He noted that takeaways usually come in bunches and that the team has to clean up ball security, mentioning Davison Igbinosun.
Brady called this the team's best win of the season given the short turnaround and travel after Monday Night Football. He praised the group's competitive stamina at 8-1.

title: Dave Canales: 'We've got to celebrate these wins'
headline: Panthers beat the Saints on the road and take sole possession of first in the NFC South. Chuba Hubbard was the offensive engine, and the defense held New Orleans to 2.1 yards per rush.
summary: Canales was thrilled with the road win and the traveling fans. He praised a defense that held the Saints to 2.1 yards per rush and limited explosive passes. The offense had missed opportunities but finished the game-winning drive, helped by Bryce Young's big downfield shot to Jalen Coker that drew a pass interference penalty. He called Chuba Hubbard a leader who 'wanted this one bad', and Hubbard broke tackles on checkdowns and in the run game. Carolina committed a franchise-record 17 penalties, and Canales said the controllable ones (offsides, delay of game, pre-snap) must be eliminated; he would not discuss the 17-to-3 penalty disparity. He trusted kicker Ryan Fitzgerald on the long field goal despite an up-and-down day, and a basic power run to the right side converted a fourth-down touchdown. Chau Smith-Wade got more snaps outside with Will Lee out, and Canales said he played excellently again. He liked that Young protected the ball without a touchdown pass, and noted Darren Waller nearly had another TD.

injuries.detail: Canales said Will 'didn't make it for the game', which opened outside CB snaps for Chau Smith-Wade.

signals.claim: Hubbard remains a featured playmaker; he touched the ball six straight plays on a late drive because he was playing well.
signals.note: Hubbard is the focal point of the offense in key moments and is trusted in the run game and as a checkdown target.
signals.quote: I just love that he's one of our leaders.

signals.note: Young had no TD pass but protected the ball and made good decisions, which Canales values; he could have had another TD.
signals.quote: I was proud of the way he took care of the ball.

signals.claim: Coker is a downfield target Young will trust on contested shots.
signals.note: Coker drew the game-changing pass interference on a deep shot, and Canales said he would have caught it without contact.
signals.quote: If they don't run into him, Jalen's going to catch that ball

signals.note: Waller had a touchdown in his hands and missed it, so he is still getting looks in scoring spots.
signals.quote: Darren kind of had it in his hands earlier.

signals.claim: Smith-Wade got more snaps outside and competes with Corey Thornton for those opportunities, with Will Lee out.
signals.note: Relevant for IDP: he has now played well two weeks in a row and may keep a bigger role while Lee is out.
signals.quote: he played excellent today again.

signals.note: Phillips was disruptive with pressures in the backfield, which is positive for IDP.
signals.quote: Jalen was all over the place

signals.note: Brown anchored a run defense that held New Orleans to 2.1 yards per carry.
signals.quote: I thought was dominant in the run game

topics.detail: Carolina set a franchise record with 17 penalties. Canales wants to eliminate controllable ones (offsides, delay of game, pre-snap). He declined to comment on the 17-to-3 disparity.

Canales said he trusts Fitzgerald, who is working through some things after an up-and-down day. He chose the field goal over going for it because Fitzgerald started onto the field with confidence, and Fitzgerald made the long kick.
A basic power run off tackle to the right side scored on fourth down. Canales said they trust their right side on that play and liked how the Saints were structured.
Todd Wash mixed looks and had a good plan for Chris Olave and the Saints' speedy receivers. The defense limited explosive passes and kept its focus all game.
The win gave Carolina sole possession of first place in the division, which Canales called their number one goal.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | Week 10 vs. Houston Texans
headline: Browns beat Houston 27-24 to reach 6-4 before the bye. Harold Fannin Jr. was a vertical weapon, the coach wants more early targets for him, and Denzel Boston played through a toe injury.
summary: Monken praised his team's resilience after it fell behind 17-0 and rallied to win 27-24, improving to 6-4 and 4-0 at home heading into the bye. He admitted the team has to start faster, since the offense struggled early with drops, missed throws and three-and-outs. He called the win-or-lose stretch a credit to the players' fight and the coaching staff. Deshaun Watson led another fourth-quarter game-winning drive. Monken said he tells Watson every week to be aggressive and let the ball rip. He singled out Harold Fannin Jr.'s 30-yard catch-and-run against a one-high look that the team had practiced all week. He said Fannin was a captain this week and didn't get enough touches early last week, but the staff tried to get him the ball early this time. Jerry Jeudy's long play (about 65 yards) sparked the offense after an early drop. Monken said the goal-line runs worked because they were more in the team's wheelhouse, and he was pleased with the offensive line despite a few protection hiccups. Denzel Boston fought through a toe injury to play and returned punts, and Monken said he had no hesitation using a top receiver there. The Browns now have a bye and then host the Raiders in two weeks.

injuries.detail: Was questionable with a toe injury but played and returned punts. Monken said the medical staff was unsure during the week, but Boston insisted on playing.

signals.claim: Fannin will keep being targeted early and on vertical routes as a featured weapon in the offense.
signals.note: Monken called him a weapon and admitted not feeding him enough early last week, so a bigger target share is likely after the bye.
signals.quote: he's such a weapon for us

signals.claim: The Browns will keep pushing Watson to throw aggressively downfield.
signals.note: Monken says he asks Watson to let it rip every week, and the deep shot to Fannin worked, which supports more downfield attempts despite slow starts.
signals.quote: I'm saying that to him every week.

signals.note: Jeudy's long catch of about 65 yards was the spark for the offense, though he also had an early drop, so his production is boom-or-bust.
signals.quote: Jerry did a great job of tracking it and catching up to it.

signals.claim: Boston will keep playing, including punt returns, despite the toe injury.
signals.note: He played through the toe issue and got a special-teams role, so his health is worth tracking, but he looks like a full participant for now.
signals.quote: I'm going to play. I'm going to play.

topics.detail: Monken said the team has to figure out how to start faster after falling behind 17-0, citing dropped passes, misses and early three-and-outs against Houston's blitzes.
He said the line did a good job against a strong pass rush, with a few missed twist pickups. He also credited chips and getting the ball out quickly.
The team ran well near the goal line this week, which he said was more in its wheelhouse than last week's struggles. No individual backs were named.
The Browns are 6-4 and 4-0 at home, 6-2 in one-score games, and now have a bye week before they come back to play better.
Monken said momentum swung in the second half and the defense played well apart from one third-and-15 interference call. He did not single out the defensive backs.

title: Campbell on Week 10 performance
headline: Aidan Hutchinson went down injured in the Munich win and Campbell has no update until the team is back in the States; Derrick Moore is the pass-rusher to watch.
summary: Campbell praised the effort and energy in the Week 10 win over New England in Munich. He treated it as a home game because of the crowd support. He singled out Amon-Ra St. Brown's early big play and touchdown run as a spark. He credited the offensive line for getting off the ball and the defense for five sacks and shutting down the run. He said "Gibbs will do the rest" once the line blocks well. On Aidan Hutchinson's injury he had nothing new and said they would know more once back in the States, adding that the team has responded before when he went down. He said Derrick Moore improves every game and that it was good to get him back. He also praised the interior rushers and said the defensive backs played sticky coverage, though the group needs others to step up now. He framed the rest of the season as a three-game schedule, with the next game at home against Tampa Bay. He also said a team member who missed the trip, who sounds like Jack Campbell, is in good spirits and improving.

injuries.detail: Went down during the game. Campbell said there was nothing new and they would know more when the team returns to the States. He called Hutchinson a captain who doesn't stay down long.
Campbell said it was good to get him back in the game, which suggests he had missed time.

The reporter's name ("Jack Kemp") is garbled and probably means Jack Campbell. A team member who didn't travel to Munich is in good spirits and getting better daily; the reason he missed the trip wasn't stated.

signals.claim: Hutchinson's injury diagnosis will be known after the team returns to the US; his availability for Tampa Bay is uncertain.
signals.note: A top pass rusher is hurt with no timeline, so IDP managers should check his status before Tampa Bay.
signals.quote: we'll know more when we get back in

signals.claim: Moore will keep getting pass-rush reps and improving, and may take on a bigger role if Hutchinson misses time.
signals.note: He is the most likely beneficiary of snaps if Hutchinson is out, which matters for IDP.
signals.quote: Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets he gets better.

signals.claim: A strong run-blocking line gives Gibbs room to produce, and the run game will keep leaning on him.
signals.note: Campbell tied the line's run-blocking to Gibbs' production, which supports his RB1 outlook.
signals.quote: You put a hat on a hat. Gibbs will do the rest.

signals.note: He made the early big play (a catch, a missed tackle and a touchdown run) after being on the injury report with a rib issue, so he looks healthy.
signals.quote: saint's big catch man makes somebody miss.

topics.detail: Five sacks and a shutdown of New England's run game. Campbell praised the interior rushers (Gill-Howard, Tyleik Williams, McNeill, Onwuzurike, Lacy) and said the secondary played sticky coverage.
Campbell said the line really showed up, got off the ball and set up the run game.
Detroit is treating the rest of the season as a three-game stretch, with the first game against New England already won. The team flies back right away and will make no excuses about the travel.

title: Matt LaFleur: ‘Today, we got humbled’
headline: Packers get blown out 30-10 by Minnesota: eight sacks and four turnovers, with the pass protection in question and Aaron Banks demoted from the starting lineup.
summary: LaFleur said Green Bay was humbled by a good Vikings team. The Packers turned the ball over four times to Minnesota's one, and he said they were out-coached and out-executed. Pass protection was the main problem. He cited busts, a missed block on Van Ginkel off the edge, and Minnesota's ultra-aggressive, multi-look pressure scheme under Flores. He admitted it was a bad decision not to use the quicker passing game until the second half, because Jordan Love was getting hit as much as in the first meeting. The longer-developing throws were taken away by the Vikings' hard outside leverage on the receivers, and the offense did not find the inside holes. LaFleur said the offensive line was shuffled: Banks did not start, someone he called Lincoln moved back to his natural spot, and Banks will compete at right guard. He still has confidence in the kicker after another miss, and said the whole team was frustrated by the eight sacks. He called the 15-yard penalty decision on third down a roll of the dice, and he framed the rest of the season as one week at a time, with seven guaranteed games left.

signals.claim: Banks will compete for the right guard job rather than being the set starter after not starting vs. Minnesota.
signals.note: A demotion on a struggling line, and a sign the blocking unit is unsettled, which hurts the Packers' run and pass efficiency.
signals.quote: we're going to let banks compete at the right guard.

signals.claim: Green Bay will need to use more quick-game concepts earlier to get the ball out of Love's hands after eight sacks and turnovers.
signals.note: Love was under constant pressure, so his fantasy value depends on pass protection improving or a quicker, shorter passing approach.
signals.quote: our quarterback was getting abused just like he did in the first game.

topics.detail: Green Bay allowed eight sacks. LaFleur pointed to blocking busts, a missed block on Van Ginkel, and Minnesota's pressure from multiple angles. He also said some of the play designs were long-developing throws that hurt the line.

Asked whether this line is sustainable, LaFleur said 'No. We'll see' and fell back on a week-to-week answer. The line was reshuffled for this game, with one lineman moved back to his natural position.

Green Bay lost the turnover battle 4-1, starting with a fumble on the second play of the game. LaFleur said the offense could not afford to waste scoring chances against one of the league's best defenses.
After another miss from the kicker (named Trey), LaFleur said he still has a lot of confidence in him, and that the team has to convert points in tight, low-scoring games.
LaFleur called Flores's scheme ultra-aggressive with many dual-call plays. The Vikings disguised their looks well and took away the outside throws with hard leverage on the receivers.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Penalties, C.J. Stroud & Quick Turnaround | Full Q&A
headline: Woody Marks is in the concussion protocol and likely out Thursday vs. the Colts. David Montgomery and Danielle Hunter have uncertain statuses after the loss to the Browns.
summary: Ryans said the Texans lost to the Browns after leading by 17 because they hurt themselves. They had 13 penalties across all three phases, including false starts, holding and a personal foul for headbutting. The offense stalled in the second half against heavy pressure, going nowhere in the third quarter. Houston converted only 3 third downs while Cleveland went 7 of 15, which he said tilted the game. Ryans blamed himself for the late defensive collapse and said he has to call it better. He also cited missed tackles, weak run defense and Deshaun Watson's scrambling as problems. He was still happy with C.J. Stroud, who made plays and kept drives alive under pressure without taking many sacks. On injuries, Woody Marks has a concussion and probably won't play Thursday. Danielle Hunter has a hamstring injury and Will Anderson an ankle issue, though Anderson was described as fine. Ryans was noncommittal on Montgomery's availability. The team turns around quickly to face the Colts on Thursday night.

injuries.detail: Diagnosed with a concussion and in the protocol. Ryans said he probably won't be available Thursday because there isn't enough time.
Ryans was unsure whether he can play Thursday ('We'll see'). The injury report listed him with a groin issue.
Hamstring injury. Ryans would only say they'll take it one day at a time.
Popped up on the report with an ankle issue, but Ryans said he was fine.

signals.claim: Marks will likely miss Thursday night's game against the Colts while in the concussion protocol.
signals.note: He is unlikely to play on a short week, which shifts backfield touches to the other healthy backs.
signals.quote: probably won't have him for Thursday night

signals.claim: Montgomery's availability for Thursday night is uncertain.
signals.note: With Marks likely out, Montgomery's status is the key variable for Houston's backfield on Thursday.
signals.quote: I'm not certain if David can play or not.

signals.claim: Hunter's hamstring injury will be handled day to day, with no timeline given for Thursday.
signals.note: The short week makes his availability uncertain, which matters for Houston's pass-rush production.
signals.quote: We'll take it one day at a time

signals.note: Ryans praised Stroud's poise and decision-making under heavy pressure, with scrambles for first downs and few sacks.
signals.quote: I'm still happy with how he played.

topics.detail: Houston had 13 penalties, including pre-snap fouls, holding and a personal foul. Ryans called most of them controllable and said the team needs a deeper look at the inconsistency. He questioned the flag on a defender named Kamara (unclear which player) for going up for the ball.
Houston converted only 3 third downs while the Browns went 7 of 15. That kept the Texans' offense off the field and let Cleveland extend drives.

Cleveland brought more pressure in the second half and Houston couldn't adjust quickly enough. The running and passing games both need to be better, and Ryans pointed to the third quarter as a particular problem.
Ryans took responsibility for play-calling on the late defensive collapse. He cited the run defense and tackling, and Deshaun Watson's scrambles while Houston was in match coverage.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Dolphins postgame
headline: Colts beat Miami 24-22. Daniel Jones stays the starter on a short week despite a stalled passing game, and Seth McGowan and Jonathan Taylor are a tagged 1-2 punch in a run-heavy offense.
summary: Steichen was glad to end the losing streak and praised the defense, especially CJ Allen's tackles, a late fourth-down sack, and a strip sack and recovery. He said the run game was strong, with McGowan finishing the four-minute offense and Taylor supplying explosive runs. Asked repeatedly about a quarterback change, he said Daniel Jones will start this week on a short week. He did not give a clear bar for a switch beyond taking care of the football, and he described the pick six as a play that went off Andrew Ogletree's hands. He admitted the passing game isn't explosive enough, with the second half limited to short throws at the line of scrimmage. He said he has to call better plays to get Tyler Warren the ball, and that coverage sometimes dictates where it goes. Laquon Treadwell scored a contested slant touchdown. On whether Anthony Richardson's legs could help the offense, Steichen said "potentially" and that they'll look at everything. He called the 13 penalties unacceptable. He also read off injuries at the start, but the captions garbled them, so only a Bernhard Raimann concussion is clear.

injuries.detail: Coach opened the press conference with a concussion for him (the captions render it "Raymond concussion"). No timeline was given.

Several other injuries were rattled off at the start ("Mooney. Ward. Shin and then Soares had a calf"), but the captions are too garbled to tell who is meant. A calf injury was mentioned for one player.

signals.claim: Jones will start at quarterback in Week 11 on the short week.
signals.note: His job is safe for now, but the coach offered no strong endorsement and the passing offense is stagnant, so the upside is capped and a change is possible.
signals.quote: Right now Daniel Jones is our quarterback.

signals.claim: McGowan will keep a significant share of carries, including late-game and four-minute situations, alongside Jonathan Taylor.
signals.note: He is earning a real role in a run-first offense and also returns kicks, which raises his weekly floor.
signals.quote: He's so explosive going through the line of scrimmage.

signals.claim: Taylor stays the explosive-play back in a split backfield, with some plays tagged so McGowan or Taylor gets the carry.
signals.note: The coach described a shared backfield, so Taylor's volume may be shared with McGowan despite his big-play ability.
signals.quote: So it's a good one two punch combo back there.

signals.claim: The staff intends to call plays to get Warren more involved, but coverage may still dictate targets.
signals.note: The coach admitted Warren hasn't been featured enough, which suggests possible upside but no guarantee.
He scored a contested slant touchdown, his first in years, amid a thin receiver group, but the coach spoke about it as a feel-good moment rather than a role change.
signals.quote: couldn't be more proud of him

signals.claim: Allen will keep wearing the green dot and playing a big defensive role.
signals.note: For IDP leagues, he is the signal-caller with heavy tackle production and a growing role.
signals.quote: he's flying around. I mean he's making a ton of plays

signals.note: Three pass breakups from an interior lineman are impressive but not a stable IDP production source.
signals.quote: Yeah he had three of them today.

signals.claim: The coaching staff may consider using Richardson's running ability in the offense.
signals.note: The coach left the door open, but a response to a hypothetical question isn't a commitment to a role or a quarterback change.
signals.quote: Yeah potentially. You know that's that's a real thing.

topics.detail: Steichen acknowledged the lack of explosive plays, with only four second-half completions all at the line of scrimmage. He said the team must be better around Jones and keep looking at how to improve.

The team had 13 penalties, which he called terrible and unacceptable, including a hold that wiped out a CJ Allen touchdown. He said taking care of the football is the key factor when evaluating the quarterback, and he described the pick six as going off Ogletree's hands.
The defense won the game late with a fourth-down sack and a strip sack by Justin Walley that was recovered. Steichen said the run game was strong and ended the losing streak.
The team has a quick turnaround to the next game, which was mentioned in the context of Jones starting.

title: Liam Coen Recaps "Good Team Win" Over Titans in Week 10 | Press Conference
headline: Parker Washington was the best player on the field in a 40-23 win, Trevor Lawrence had one of his best games, and RB Bhayshul Tuten is playing through injury on little practice.
summary: Coen called the 40-23 win over Tennessee a good team win. He said the offense moved the ball in the first half but didn't finish drives with touchdowns, then fixed that after halftime. Jacksonville went 7-of-14 on third down while holding Tennessee to 2-of-11, and it had few penalties. Coen said Parker Washington was 'possessed' and the best player on the field, while other pass catchers such as Josh Cameron made big plays in the second half. He put Trevor Lawrence's game among the best he has seen from him, citing his accuracy, clean footwork, key scrambles and a fourth-down sneak conversion. Travis Hunter's interception and Antonio Johnson's sack in a three-point game were called huge momentum plays. Tuten, whom Coen called Teutons, is playing through an injury with very little practice and Coen said he is not 100%. Jonah Monheim came in for Robert Hainsey and was solid, though Coen wasn't sure what happened to Hainsey. Coen also said the team won without several new acquisitions who were on a makeshift bye week, and that it hopes they add to the roster down the stretch.

injuries.detail: Playing through an injury, practicing very little during the week and not 100% on game day for the last two weeks. Coen praised his toughness and said he was close to breaking a few runs.
Left the game and Jonah Monheim replaced him. Coen said he wasn't sure what happened. Hainsey was listed as questionable with a concussion this week.

signals.claim: Washington remains a go-to receiver in the passing game and was the offense's best player on Sunday.
signals.note: Coen's praise and his description of Washington winning on every ball back up a high target share and WR1-type usage.
signals.quote: Parker was definitely the best player on the field today.

signals.claim: Lawrence is playing at a very high level, accurate and effective as both a passer and runner on scrambles and sneaks.
signals.note: Coen called it one of the better games he has seen from Lawrence, and the scrambles and sneak add rushing upside to his fantasy floor.
signals.quote: I thought that he was extremely accurate for the most part of the day

signals.claim: Tuten will keep playing through the injury with limited practice during the week.
signals.note: He is productive but not healthy, so his week-to-week status depends on how the injury and practice participation go.
signals.quote: He's not perfect. He's not, um, you know, 100%.

signals.claim: Cameron was targeted on the first third down of the game and made a critical sideline catch late.
signals.note: He earned the quarterback's trust on key downs, which could mean a bigger role in the passing game.

signals.claim: Monheim stepped in for Hainsey and the offense kept moving the ball efficiently.
signals.note: If Hainsey misses time, Monheim looks capable, so the offensive line should hold up for the skill players.
signals.quote: when Jonah came in, we were able to continue to move the football

signals.note: Hunter made a huge interception right after a Jacksonville turnover, a defensive playmaking plus for IDP formats.
signals.quote: unbelievable catch, unbelievable play

signals.note: His sack in a three-point game knocked Tennessee out of field goal range, a notable IDP play.
signals.quote: AJ getting them down on the ground.

topics.detail: Jacksonville moved the ball in the first half but settled for too few touchdowns, then finished better after halftime. The team was 7-of-14 on third down, Tennessee was 2-of-11, and Lawrence's scramble on a critical third-and-long was singled out.
Coen said Cam Little continued to kick at a very high level and the operation was clean. He credited special teams with winning the hidden-yards battle.
A well-timed blitz call by the defensive coordinator, which Coen briefly considered checking out of, led to the sack by Antonio Johnson in a three-point game.

Coen said the team played well without several new acquisitions, including players named Jesse, Jordan and Davon, who were on a makeshift bye week. He hopes they add to the team during a late-season push.
Coen said the offense threw well and ran better in the second half, and said any skill player can step up on a given week. That makes weekly usage harder to predict.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Win Over Packers, Kirk Cousins’ Performance & Vikings Outstanding Defense
headline: Kirk Cousins ran the offense cleanly in a win over Green Bay on just two full days of work, and young pass catchers like Myles Price, Gavin Bartholomew, Ben Yurosek and Tai Felton stepped into big roles.
summary: O'Connell was very happy with a complementary win at Lambeau, praising the defense and the way the team leaned into the run game. He gave most of the credit to Kirk Cousins, who arrived mid-week, owned the game plan and brought poise and leadership. Cousins had only Thursday and Friday for full practices, yet he threw touchdowns to receivers he had never played with. O'Connell highlighted an 11-play drive in which Cousins went 8-for-8, including six straight throws to Justin Jefferson. Jefferson drew a defender on him everywhere, with a safety over the top, so the offense had to make plays around him without letting him disappear. Young players Bartholomew, Yurosek, Price and Felton were praised for stepping into major roles, and Price's touchdown catch was singled out. O'Connell also admitted that some screen calls were not good ones and that the offense still has plenty to clean up. On injuries, a player he called Richter (foot) did not return, and Jeshaun Jones (shoulder) returned but will likely get an MRI. He also said his two starting tight ends from training camp are out, one likely for the season.

injuries.detail: Hurt his shoulder but returned to the game; likely to have an MRI to check its status.
Coach said a player named Richter had a foot injury and did not return, with no further update. He does not match anyone clearly on the roster.
Coach said his two starting tight ends from camp are out, one likely for the season, and did not name them in this session.

signals.claim: Cousins is the Vikings' quarterback going forward, with O'Connell calling plays for him.
signals.note: Cousins looked comfortable and efficient on short prep, which is good for the passing game's outlook.
signals.quote: ran the show incredibly clean

signals.claim: Opponents will keep a safety over the top of Jefferson, and the offense will look to make plays around him while still targeting him.
signals.note: Cousins fed Jefferson six straight times on the key drive, but heavy coverage may cap his volume in some games.
signals.quote: Justin was going to have a human being with him everywhere he went

signals.claim: Price is in a major receiving role and made a high-timing touchdown catch and run.
signals.note: He earned Cousins' trust with a touchdown and may keep a role in a thin receiver group.
signals.quote: unbelievable execution in that moment

signals.claim: Bartholomew is stepping into a major tight end role with the starting tight ends out.
signals.note: With the top tight ends out, he is a streaming candidate if the role continues.
signals.quote: stepping up into major, major roles under the circumstances

signals.claim: Yurosek is playing a major role at tight end while the starters are out.
signals.note: He is part of the thin tight end rotation and could carry some value if snaps stay high.

signals.claim: Felton is stepping into a major role in the receiver group.
signals.note: He is worth watching as a deep-league receiver while injuries limit the group.

topics.detail: O'Connell said the team leaned into the running game some and won the field-position, turnover and time-of-possession battles. He called it one of the first times this year the team played complementary football.

O'Connell said the screens looked similar but were different, and that execution and physicality could have been better. He said a couple of the calls were not good ones by him while protecting a lead.

He credited the defense's variety of looks and one-on-one wins on four-man rushes, naming Dallas Turner, the interior linemen and Andrew Van Ginkel. He also credited the defensive staff for mixing the pressures.

He praised Ryan Cordell for the replay challenge that kept Green Bay pinned. Cordell is also coaching tight ends from the box with the starters out, and Devin Culp joined the team a couple of weeks ago.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 11/15: "We all have to recognize what we need to do better"
headline: Drake Maye left the 35-10 loss to Detroit with a lower-leg injury and AJ Brown also didn't finish. The bye is next, and Tommy DeVito is the fallback at QB if Maye misses time.
summary: Mike Vrabel said the Patriots lost 35-10 to the Lions in Munich and have now allowed about 80 points over two straight losses. Drake Maye did not finish the game. Vrabel called it a lower-leg injury, said he doesn't know the exact details, and said more tests are coming when the team returns. He said Maye couldn't function well enough to go back in, and he gave no clear timeline. AJ Brown also did not finish the game, and Vrabel offered no update beyond waiting to see the severity. Tommy DeVito replaced Maye, and Vrabel said the game plan didn't need to change because the backup quarterbacks can run everything. He pointed to the real problems: missed tackles, too many clean pockets for the opposing QB, offensive turnovers, and drives the offense ended itself. He said a bye is coming, the team will be in on Tuesday, and what happens there depends on the injuries. He framed the team as 0-0 heading out of the bye and said it needs a winner's mentality. He also said the team has to fix things itself rather than expect a pep talk.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a lower-leg injury and could not return. Vrabel said more tests are needed and he doesn't know the exact details.
Did not finish the game. Vrabel said the severity is still unknown until the team gets back and evaluates him.

signals.claim: Maye will undergo more tests after the team returns; his availability after the bye is unknown.
signals.note: A lower-leg injury that forced him out of the game makes his post-bye availability a key fantasy question for the QB and his pass catchers.
signals.quote: I know that it was a lower leg injury.

signals.claim: Brown's injury severity will be determined after the team returns from Munich.
signals.note: He left the game early and the coach gave no timeline, so his status after the bye is uncertain.
signals.quote: We'll see what uh, you know, the severity of that is.

signals.claim: DeVito replaced Maye mid-game and could be the quarterback if Maye misses time.
signals.note: If Maye is out, DeVito's limited experience makes the passing game a downgrade, though Vrabel says the full playbook is available to him.
signals.quote: those quarterbacks are able to execute everything that we want to do

signals.note: Vrabel praised Gonzalez's response after a poor week, citing his interception and effort to force a turnover, which is relevant for IDP.
signals.quote: it's good to see him come back and respond

topics.detail: Vrabel cited missed tackles, too many clean pockets for the opposing QB and not enough effort at the finish. He said there are glimpses of good play but not enough, and that the defense wasn't helping each other tackle.
Vrabel said the offense has to stop turning the ball over and has to run the football, get open and catch the ball, and protect the quarterback. He said the offense often ended its own drives.
The team will be in on Tuesday and Vrabel is unsure what practice will look like given the injured players. He called the bye a reset and the team 0-0.
Vrabel said the losses start with him and said there is no magic formula or pep talk. He wants a winner's mentality and said the team must do its job and get back to work.

title: Kellen Moore | Saints-Panthers Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 10
headline: Saints lost 2-0 in turnovers to Carolina, and the run game and offense stalled. Jordyn Tyson got extra targets because Carolina's coverage focused on Chris Olave, Travis Etienne returned from his hamstring injury, and Pete Werner left with a left hamstring injury.
summary: Kellen Moore called the loss self-inflicted. He said the defense battled and special teams helped, but the offense was not good enough, with two turnovers, no takeaways and several penalties. He took responsibility for the stalled run game ('I wasn't able to create that') and said he should have been more aggressive at the end. The Saints went for the win on the last drive rather than a tying field goal, then kicked on fourth down. He said Jordyn Tyson saw more targets than normal because of how Carolina played coverage on Chris Olave. Moore said Tyler Shough is 'playing fine' and battling, and put the offense's struggles on his own play-calling and preparation. He praised Travis Etienne's return, saying he found yards when there was nothing there. He also acknowledged a fumble on a run/throw exchange involving Audric Estime. Defensively he cited missed tackles on a check-down and a screen to Chuba Hubbard. Pete Werner has a left hamstring injury and the team is still gathering information. Moore named turnovers, sustaining drives and running the football as the offense's main problems.

injuries.detail: Left hamstring injury. Moore said the team is still collecting information, so the severity is unknown.
Listed out with a biceps injury. A reporter asked about his absence, and Moore said other players had opportunities.
Listed out with a knee injury. The reporter's 'Tyler' may mean him, but that is not certain.
Played after being listed questionable with a hamstring injury. Moore was positive about his performance.

signals.claim: Tyson got more targets than normal because of how Carolina played coverage.
signals.note: He benefited from defenders focusing on Olave. This is a matchup-driven bump, not a stated change in role.
signals.quote: the ball ended up in Jordan's hands a few more times

signals.claim: Olave is still the starting point on many designed plays, but defenses are taking him away.
signals.note: Heavy coverage on Olave can cut his volume and raise Tyson's.
signals.quote: He's the starting point for the play.

signals.claim: Etienne is back playing after his hamstring issue.
signals.note: He was effective enough in a bad rushing game that his role looks safe.
signals.quote: I thought he battled. I thought he did some good things.

signals.note: A fumble on a run/throw exchange hurts his standing, though Moore framed it as a team exchange issue.
signals.quote: we just can't have the ball on the ground.

signals.note: Moore called him fine and put the blame on his own play-calling, but the offense is struggling.
signals.quote: He's playing fine. He's battling.

signals.claim: Werner's left hamstring injury is still being evaluated.
signals.note: His availability is in doubt, which matters for IDP and the defense's depth at linebacker.
signals.quote: they're collecting information right now

topics.detail: Moore said the run game was not good and gained no movement or rhythm against a good run defense. He took responsibility for not creating it and said he has to figure it out.

Moore said the last drive was meant to take the lead, not to set up a tying field goal. He said he should have called it more aggressively and found a way to get the ball downfield. On fourth down he chose to kick the tying field goal and try to win in overtime.
The Saints lost the turnover battle 2-0 for the second straight week. Moore said they could not capitalize on Carolina's penalties.
Missed tackles led to a long check-down gain and a screen for Chuba Hubbard. Moore said everyone needs to pursue the ball better and he will look at fundamental and schematic fixes.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/15) | Week 10
headline: Geno Smith and Omar Cooper Jr. both left the loss with ankle injuries, and the severity won't be known until next week. A young QB ("Cade") played in relief.
summary: Glenn was disappointed after the Week 10 loss, which left the Jets 2-8 and on a five-game losing streak. He liked the first half, but said a couple of big plays by the opponent derailed the second half. Penalties on both sides of the ball hurt too, helping put the opponent inside the five-yard line and pushing the Jets' own offense out of the red zone. He admitted the offense moves the ball well, with roughly 30 plays in opposing territory, but keeps failing to finish drives, and the team has gone nine quarters without a touchdown. Geno Smith (ankle), Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) and Dylan Parham (knee) were hurt in the game. Glenn did not know whether the ankle injuries were high or low sprains and expects more information sometime next week. He praised the young quarterback who came in ("Cade") for a strong first drive, good throws and mobility against a tough pass rush. He said he is frustrated but will not panic or make drastic changes. Players are off Tuesday, and the team will keep working on the red zone and penalties starting Wednesday.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury suffered in the game. Glenn doesn't know whether it's a high or low ankle sprain and expects more information sometime next week.
Ankle injury suffered in the game. Severity unknown, with more information expected next week. He was already listed questionable with an ankle.
Knee injury suffered in the game. No further detail given.

signals.claim: Smith's ankle injury will be evaluated, with the severity known sometime next week.
signals.note: Smith's availability for next week is in doubt, and a young backup took over at QB, so Jets passing-game values are at risk.
signals.quote: I just know they're both ankles right now.

signals.claim: Cooper's ankle injury will be evaluated, with the severity known sometime next week.
signals.note: The rookie WR was already questionable with an ankle, so monitor his practice participation before relying on him.
signals.quote: I just know they're both ankles right now.

topics.detail: The Jets move the ball between the 20s but can't finish drives, with nine quarters without a touchdown. Penalties on both sides of the ball hurt, helping put the opponent inside the five and pushing the offense out of the red zone.

Glenn praised the young quarterback ("Cade", not on the provided roster) who was thrown into the game against a strong pass rush. He cited a strong first drive, impressive throws and good mobility, but wants to review the film.
A hook-and-lateral type play involving Garrett Wilson was part of the weekly game plan and was tried at what Glenn called an opportune time. It did not work.
Glenn said he is frustrated but will not panic or make drastic moves, and he is standing by the weekly work process. Players are off Tuesday, and the team returns to the field Wednesday.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans lost 40-23 to Jacksonville; Saleh said the defense must improve and praised Cam Ward, saying the team is confident putting the ball in his hands.
summary: Saleh said the Titans' defense failed in critical moments, especially on third down (Jacksonville converted 7 of 14) and on a key third-and-11 while the game was 30-23. He said the team has now allowed 300-yard passers three games in a row and that giving up around 40 points a game won't win games. He pointed to Jacksonville's receivers making big plays, noting Washington's catches and Jakobi Meyers' quality. He also said some coverage busts, such as a cloud-coverage breakdown on the last touchdown, and slow reactions on check-downs let drives extend. Saleh disagreed with the roughing-the-passer call and a non-called pick play near the goal line, but said the officials did a good job overall. He defended the team's effort, saying the 40-23 score doesn't reflect how close the game felt. He said the opening seven straight passes were simply the game plan, and that Cam Ward is close to playing at a consistently high level.

signals.claim: The Titans will keep putting the ball in Cam Ward's hands and leaning on the passing game.
signals.note: Saleh's confidence in Ward and the pass-heavy opening (seven straight passes in tempo) supports Ward's fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: Cam has been getting a lot better throughout the course of the year

topics.detail: Saleh blamed third-down failures (7 of 14 allowed), explosive plays on third down, and missed one-on-one wins on the outside, inside and in the pass rush. He said coverage miscommunication led to the last touchdown.
Saleh disagreed with a roughing-the-passer call and a pick play near the goal line that wasn't called, but said the officials were good overall.
The Titans opened with seven straight passes in tempo because that's what the game plan called for, not as a copy of an earlier game.
